newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Ericsson down on AT&T news.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Ericsson down on AT&T news.

text.p: Swedish telephone equipment company Telefon AB L.M. Ericsson fell Tuesday, hit by concerns over AT&T Corp's reported merger talks with SBC Communications Inc, traders said.
Ericsson's American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) were off 1-2/16 at 35-13/16 in moderate trading that put it at the top of the ADR most-active list.

The Wall Street Journal reported today that AT&T, the biggest U.S. telecom carrier, and SBC, owner of the Southwestern Bell and Pacific Telesis local phone systems, were in talks for a merger worth more than $50 billion, which would be the biggest corporate combination ever.
AT&T and SBC declined comment on the report.
Ericsson "is off on the AT&T and Southwestern Bell discussions," said Val Kosmider, head of international equity trading at Schroder Wertheim.
"Bell is a big equipment provider and, presumably, if SBC and AT&T team up, a lot of what they source out" for equipment could be supplied internally, he said.
Finnish telecommunications equipment company Nokia Group also was lower, off 1-1/4 to 68-1/8.
French ADRs were down, hit by concerns that the Socialists could take over parliament.
Among oil companies, Total SA fell 2-1/8 to 47-1/4 and Elf Aquitaine was off 2-3/8 at 52-3/8. Luxury goods maker LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton fell 1-1/2 to 48-3/8.
Among Latin American ADRs, Brazilian telephone holding high of 132-1/4 on optimism over privatization and the prospect of Telebras taking a stake in Portugal Telecom .
Portugal Telecom is 1.5 percent owned by the international Concert alliance, headed by MCI Communications Corp and British Telecommunications Plc. Portugal Telecom ADRs were unchanged at 39.
Decliners led advancers 240 to 207 among 814 ADRs. The ADR group was up 0.03 percent and volume in late morning was 24.5 million ADRs.
ADRs allow U.S. trading of foreign shares.
